info.description:
LangSmith Tool Gateway lets your applications, agents, and MCP clients call MCP tools with each caller's own credentials.

## Start here
1. Register an MCP server or select a built-in integration.
2. Connect each user's OAuth account or API key when the integration requires one.
3. Optionally create a tool kit containing selected tools.
4. Call the server or tool kit MCP endpoint from your application, agent, or development environment.

## API surfaces
**Management APIs** configure Tool Gateway: `/servers` registers and lists MCP servers, `/servers/{id}/credential` manages the current user's credential, `/kits` manages curated tool kits, and `/oidc-connection` links your identity provider.

**MCP APIs** discover and invoke tools through standard MCP methods such as `tools/list` and `tools/call`: `/servers/{id}/mcp` exposes one server and `/kits/{kit_id}/mcp` exposes a tool kit.

## Choose who you're calling as
| You call as | Send |
| --- | --- |
| Yourself | A personal `X-Api-Key`, or `Authorization: Bearer {langsmith_token}`, plus `X-Tenant-Id` |
| A user, from your trusted backend | A workspace `X-Api-Key`, the user's `Authorization: Bearer {oidc_token}` (or `X-LangSmith-Identity`), and `X-Tenant-Id`. Listing servers and MCP calls only |
| An agent | An API key bound to the agent's environment as `X-Api-Key`, plus `X-Tenant-Id` |
| A profile | `X-Api-Key`, `X-LangSmith-Profile`, and `X-Tenant-Id`. Requires workspaces:credentials:use or agent-auth-credentials:use |
| A user, with your identity provider | The user's `Authorization: Bearer {oidc_token}` alone. MCP calls only; built-ins also need `X-Tenant-Id` |

`X-Tenant-Id` selects a workspace; it does not authenticate you. Service keys are not supported, except LangSmith's internal Agent Builder service key, which may list servers and make MCP calls.

## When you're not connected yet
An MCP call that needs your credential returns 428 with a `verification_url`. Open it, connect, and retry. If your client declares `elicitation.url`, you get an MCP URL elicitation instead: a -32042 error on a 2025-11-25 `initialize`, or an `input_required` result on a 2026-07-28 `tools/call`. Each names its connection in `_meta["com.langchain.langsmith/credential"]`, with `auth_id`, the session to check for completion. An agent or profile gets 409 instead; an admin connects it.

## When a call needs approval
An approval policy can require your OK before a tool runs. Tool Gateway asks through an MCP form elicitation on protocol 2026-07-28 or later and runs the call when you accept it on retry. A client that can't show the form gets 403.

## Search mode
`/kits/{kit_id}/mcp?mode=search` lists three tools, `search_tools`, `get_tool`, and `call_tool`, instead of every tool. Use it when your host puts every listed tool in the model prompt, for example with the me kit (`kit_id` = `me`). Calling a tool by name works in both modes.

Tool Gateway must be enabled for the organization. Endpoint descriptions list the required workspace permissions.

get.description: Lists the workspace's tool kits and your personal tool kits in creation order. Requires mcp-servers:read. Call as yourself. Items omit tools; get a kit to see its tools.

parameters.name: scope

403.description: Tool Gateway isn't enabled for your organization, or you lack the required permission.

post.description: Creates a tool kit, a named set of tools served through one MCP endpoint. Requires mcp-servers:invoke, plus mcp-servers:create for a workspace kit (the default), or mcp-servers:create-personal or mcp-servers:create for a personal kit (scope personal). Call as yourself. A workspace kit links only workspace MCP servers and built-ins. A personal kit can also link your personal servers and is visible only to you. Tool definitions are stored as you list them (not built-ins), so users who aren't connected still see the tools; a listing failure doesn't fail the write.

parameters.name: kit_id

delete.description: Deletes a tool kit; its MCP servers and user credentials are kept. Requires mcp-servers:delete for a workspace kit. Only the owner can delete a personal kit, with mcp-servers:create-personal or mcp-servers:create. Returns 204 if the kit is already gone.

parameters.description: Tool kit ID
parameters.name: kit_id

403.description: Tool Gateway isn't enabled for your organization, or you lack the required permission.

patch.description: Updates the fields you send and returns the tool kit. Requires mcp-servers:invoke, plus mcp-servers:update for a workspace kit, or mcp-servers:create-personal or mcp-servers:create for a personal kit. Call as yourself. Sending tools replaces the selection (an empty array or null removes all) and stores tool definitions as you list them; a listing failure doesn't fail the write. A kit keeps its scope: only a personal kit can link personal servers.

post.description: Serves a tool kit as one stateless MCP endpoint: initialize, server/discover, ping, tools/list, and tools/call. Requires mcp-servers:invoke. Tool lists are cached for 2 hours and served stale for up to 30 more minutes while they refresh. tools/list includes tools from servers you haven't connected and names each missing credential in result._meta["com.langchain.langsmith/missingCredentials"]. The me kit holds every server you can use; pair it with search mode. The API overview covers connecting, approvals, and search mode.

x-codeSamples.label: List tools with a personal API key
Call a tool with OIDC
x-codeSamples.source:
curl --request POST 'https://api.smith.langchain.com/v1/managed-tools/kits/<kit-id>/mcp' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer <oidc-access-token>' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  --header 'MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-06-18' \
  --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"<tool-name>","arguments":{}}}'

post.description: Refreshes a tool kit's MCP servers and waits for the cache to update. Requires mcp-servers:update and mcp-servers:invoke, and no ABAC deny policy on MCP servers or built-ins. Call as yourself. Also stores the servers' tool definitions as you list them (not built-ins), so users who aren't connected still see the tools. Returns 200 when every server refreshes or needs a credential; missing_credentials lists the ones you must connect. Other failures return an error but keep other servers' writes. Times out after 90 seconds.

post.description: Registers an HTTPS MCP server that is public or uses OAuth or per-user header credentials. Requires mcp-servers:create for a workspace server (the default, visible to the workspace), or mcp-servers:create-personal or mcp-servers:create for a personal server (visible only to you). Call as yourself. Selecting a shared OAuth connection also requires workspaces:integrations:manage. which every caller of the server then uses, including agents in the
workspace, and while it is stored no other owner can add one. It
requires a workspace server and workspaces:credentials:manage.

tools this credential unlocks, as MCP tool definitions. A linked server's

sees them. Calling one returns 428 until the credential is connected.

Clients must tolerate values added later. connected: the credential is usable; public servers are always connected. needs_connect: the user has no credential. needs_reconnect: the stored credential must be authorized again. unavailable: the state could not be checked; it says nothing about the credential itself.
